I wonder if Mark Burgess’ Promise Theory is a drop-in kit for this sort of thing? It’s literally constructed to enable agents to manage two-way exchange in a formally specified manner.

> Crucially, Blygger need not collect the money, determine the currency or operate the marketplace. It would standardize the grammar of the offer—bid, ask, bond, bounty, guarantee—just as HTTP standardizes requests without owning the websites using them.

[Protocol Pricing for Product People — And Yet Here We Are 🚀 ↗](https://blyg.aneeshsathe.com/t/7zz5hby5zr9t7s2be5j032p3ec)
content_html:
I wonder if Mark Burgess’ Promise Theory is a drop-in kit for this sort of thing? It’s literally constructed to enable agents to manage two-way exchange in a formally specified manner.

Crucially, Blygger need not collect the money, determine the currency or operate the marketplace. It would standardize the grammar of the offer—bid, ask, bond, bounty, guarantee—just as HTTP standardizes requests without owning the websites using them.

Protocol Pricing for Product People — And Yet Here We Are 🚀 ↗
